

Scalability

- Two types

	- Vertical Scalability
		- Upgrading size/capacity
- Horizontal Scalability
	- Increase in numbers
Availability
- Goes hand and hand with horizontal scalability
- Ability to survive a data center loss
- Application being in multiple Availability Zones (AZ)

Load Balancing

## Why an Elastic Load Balancer
- A managed load balancer by AWS
- Guarantees to work
- Takes care of upgrades, maintenance, high availability
    
- Few configurations
    

- Cost more than managing your own
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  
  

|   |   |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|
|Feature|ALB (Application)|NLB (Network)|GWLB (Gateway)|
|OSI Layer|Layer 7 (Application)|Layer 4 (Transport)|Layer 3 (Network)|
|Typical Use|Web Apps / Microservices|High Performance / TCP|Firewalls / IDS|
|Static IP?|No (Uses DNS name)|Yes (Static / Elastic IP)|No|
|Latency|Higher (Smart routing)|Ultra-low|Transparent|
|Cross-Zone|Enabled by default|Disabled by default ($$$)|Disabled by default ($$$)|

  

Application Load Balancer

- ALB great fit for micro services & container-based applications (Docker & Amazon ECS)
    

- Web applications
    

- Port Mapping feature for dynamic port redirection in ECS
    

- HTTP/HTTPS. And WebSockets
    

- Key “Logic” features
    

- Path-based routing
    

- Sending traffic to “Images” group if URL is /images 
    

- Videos too
    

- Host-based routing
    

- Based on Domain Name Service (DNS)
    

- SNI (Server Name Indication)
    

- Allows to host multiple SSL Certifications for different websites on a single ALB
    

- Sticky Sessions: Keeps users stuck/connected to the same backend server during sessions. (No lag when, no reconnecteding to a different server ever time)
    
- Identifying Cliets: acts as a proxy, backend server sees the ALB’s IP.
    

- Use X-Forwarded-For header to see the actual client’s IP address
    

  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Target Groups: can route to multiple target groups
    

- EC2
    
- ECS
    
- Lambda Functions
    
- IP Addresses (Private IP’s)
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  

Network Load Balancer (V2)

- Forward TCP & UDP traffic to instances
    

- Also handles TLS (Secure TCP)
    
- Used for extreme performance, TCP or UDP Traffic
    

- Handle Millions of Request per seconds
    
- Ultra-low latency
    
- One static IP per AZ and supports assigning Elastic IP (helpful for whitelisting specific IP)
    

- Preserves the client’s source IP address natively
    

- Backend servers see the real user’s IP Directly
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  

Gateway Load Balancer- “The Security Guard”

- Newest load balancer
    
- Best for: Scaling and managing 3rd party virtual appliances like Firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS/IPS), or Deep Packet Inspection tools
    
- Operates at Layer 3 (Network Layer - IP Packets)
    
- Analyzes network traffic
    
- Combines the following functions:
    

- Transparent Network Gateway - single entry/exit for all traffic
    
- Load Balancer - distributes traffic to your virtual appliances
    

- Uses GENEVE protocol on port 6081

Cross-Zone Load Balancing

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Application Load Balancer
    

- Enabled by default (can be disabled at the Target Group Level)
    
- No Charges for inter AZ data
    

- Network Load Balancer & Gateway Load Balancer
    

- Disabled by default
    
- $$$ for inter AZ data if enabled
    

SSL/TLS Basic

- SSL Certificate allows traffic between your clients and your load balancer to be encrypted in transit (in-flight encryption)
    

- SSL refers to Secure Sockets Layer
    

- Encrypts connections
    
- Older version
    

- TLS refers to Transport Layer Security Security
    

- Newer version of SSL
    
- Mainly used today
    

- Public SSL certificates are used by Certificate Authorities (CA)
    

- Comodo, Symantec, GoDaddy, GlobalSign
    

- SSL Certificates have an expiration date and must be renewed.
    

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Elastic Load Balancers - SSL Certificates

- Application Load Balancers (V2)
    

- Supports multiple listeners with multiple SSL certificates
    
- Uses Server Name Indication (SNI) to make it work
    

- Network Load Balancers
    

- Supports multiple listeners with multiple SSL certificates
    
- Uses Server Name Indication (SNI) to make it work
    

Auto Scaling Group

- Scale out (add EC2 Instance) to match an increase load
    
- Scale in (remove EC2) to match a decreased load.
    
- Has a minimum and maximum number of EC2 Instances
    
- Automatically register new instances to a load balancer
    
- Re-create a EC2 instance in case a previous one is terminated (ex: if unhealthy)
    
- ASG are free

- Auto Scaling Groups - Scaling Policies
    

- Dynamic Scaling
    

- Target Tracking Scaling
    

- Simple to set-up
    

- Simple/Step Scaling
    

- When CloudWatch alarm is triggered, add units (Step up)
    
- When a CloudWatch alarm is triggered, remove 1 unit.
    

- Scheduled Scaling
    

- Anticipate a scaling based on known usage patterns
